home.title: AquaShield: AI leak detection for buildings
home.description: AquaShield detects and localizes leaks in complex pipe networks using non-invasive sensors and AI. Clamp-on, no pipe cutting, riser-level localization.

product.title: How AquaShield works: sensors, AI, digital twin

product.lead: Sensors clamp onto your pipes and our models learn how water moves through each building. When something changes, your team gets a riser and a floor.

visual.alt: Diagram: a clamp-on sensor on a pipe sends readings into a live-flow chart with its learned baseline, a deviation is placed on the building's digital twin and raised as an alert.

install.h2: What does an install look like?
install.text: Each sensor clamps onto an existing pipe in about 30 seconds while the water stays on. Your own team can do it.
install.visualAlt: Diagram: clamp-on sensors on a riser and on the supply line that feeds it.

data.text: One dashboard with live flow for every measuring point. Our models learn each building's normal flow and flag what it does not explain. Each alert names the building and the riser.

precision.text: To the riser or the building section, so the search starts on the right floors.

ml.visualAlt: Measuring points, each with its learned baseline band and live flow. One riser departs from its baseline and is flagged.

sensors.intro: It reads the flow through the pipe wall, so the pipe is never opened.

visual.alt: A clamp-on sensor on the outside of a pipe. Its signal crosses the water flowing inside.

twin.text: The digital twin: a model of the building's plumbing that turns a deviation into a place to look.

faq.q: Does the install interrupt the water supply?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto the outside of the pipe and the water stays on.

faq.q: How long does a rollout take?
faq.a: A building is live in a day. Each sensor clamps on in about 30 seconds with no shutdown, and your own team can install them, so many buildings go live in parallel.
You and the people you name. We do not sell data, see the privacy policy.
Priced per building and measuring point, a fraction of one claim. We quote from your plumbing plan.

twinModel.caption: Risers, branches and sensors of a building, as our model sees them. Click a sensor and you see its flow.
twinModel.alt: 3D model of a ten-floor building with four risers, branches on every floor and clamp-on sensors on the risers.

realEstate.h1: Find the leak before your tenant does.
realEstate.lead: For portfolio teams with in-house maintenance, from a few hundred units to hundreds of thousands.

visual.alt: Six buildings of a portfolio, each watched by a riser sensor. One building shows a deviation on riser B and an alert names the floors to look at.

story.h2: Most leaks are found by a tenant.
story.text: Usually through a call or a stained ceiling, days or weeks after the leak started. AquaShield watches every riser and sends your team an alert like this one.

steps.name: Map
steps.text: Send us the plumbing plan. We place the sensors and build the twin.

steps.name: Install
steps.text: About 30 seconds per sensor while the water stays on.

steps.name: Learn
steps.text: The model learns the building's normal flow.

steps.name: Detect
steps.text: Alerts are ranked by severity and name the riser.

faq.q: We have smart water meters. Is this the same?
faq.a: No. Meters count use per unit, while AquaShield learns normal flow at the riser and catches leaks no single meter sees.

faq.q: Do we need to open walls?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto accessible pipe in risers and basements.

faq.q: What does our maintenance team have to do?
faq.a: Clamp on the sensors, or let us do it. Then act on the alerts, each one names a riser and the floors.
One. Roll out when you have seen it work.

realEstate.live: Live in 25+ buildings in Europe and the US. Research with MIT and EPFL facilities.

insurance.h1: Shorter loss duration. Lower claim severity.
insurance.lead: For property underwriters and claims teams who want shorter losses and better risk data.

story.lead: A hidden leak runs until someone notices, and every extra day adds secondary damage.

timeline.alt: Timeline. Without monitoring, a hidden leak runs for weeks. It reaches the subfloor, the drywall, the neighboring unit and business interruption before a tenant discovers it. With AquaShield, a flow deviation is flagged early, the riser is located and the rest of the loss is avoided.

levers.name: Lever 1: shorter loss duration
levers.text: Fewer days of water mean less secondary damage and a smaller claim.

levers.name: Lever 2: a live risk signal
levers.text: Flow data per riser gives underwriting a signal it does not have today.

dataCenters.h1: Detect the leak before the outage happens.
dataCenters.lead: For operations leads running liquid cooling, where the real cost is the outage.

visual.alt: Diagram: a row of liquid-cooled racks on one cooling loop, a clamp-on flow sensor on every rack branch, one branch showing a flow deviation.

story.h2: Floor leak cables tell you after the fact.
story.lead: A leak cable fires once water reaches the floor and a rack has already lost cooling. AquaShield watches the loop itself.

cable.title: Leak cable
steps: A leak starts in the loop.
Water reaches the floor. The cable fires.
The rack has already lost cooling.

aqua.title: AquaShield
steps: A leak starts in the loop.
Flow on one branch stops matching its neighbors.
The alert names the rack and the branch.
You act before the rack loses cooling.

how.h2: How it works on a cooling loop.

steps.name: Clamp on
steps.text: Sensors clamp onto every rack branch while the loop keeps running.

steps.name: Learn the loop
steps.text: The model learns how each branch flows, alone and next to its neighbors.

steps.name: Flag the branch
steps.text: When one branch drifts, the alert names its rack.

chapters.title: The hackathon
chapters.text: Paul and Marguerite meet at an MIT hackathon and win it with AquaShield. The week after, they clamp the first sensors onto pipes in a campus building.
chapters.alt: Paul Beckers and Marguerite Benoist in front of the Great Dome at MIT.

chapters.title: Y Combinator
chapters.text: Spring 2026, months of building at full speed among people doing the same. That pace never left us, and part of us still lives in San Francisco.
chapters.alt: Marguerite Benoist and Paul Beckers behind the Y Combinator sign in San Francisco.

chapters.title: The team
chapters.text: Today we build from Zurich, one of Europe's strongest hubs for robotics and machine learning. Our models get sharper with every building, and the team grows with people who want to build them.
chapters.alt: The AquaShield team around a table of laptops in the Zurich office.
